destroyed$

The destroyed$ stream emits a single notification when a FeatureCell is permanently destroyed. This stream provides a reliable lifecycle signal that indicates the FeatureCell has been fully torn down and will no longer participate in Vault-managed execution.

Stream Contract Summary

  • Emits exactly once when the FeatureCell is destroyed
  • Completes immediately after emission
  • Signals permanent teardown of the FeatureCell
  • Never emits values during normal execution
  • Cannot emit again once completed

The destroyed$ stream defines a terminal lifecycle boundary. It does not emit state values, does not participate in pipeline execution, and does not influence control flow. Its sole responsibility is to notify subscribers that the FeatureCell lifecycle has ended.

Note

The destroyed$ stream is completed as part of the FeatureCell destruction process. Once this stream emits, the FeatureCell cannot be re-initialized or reused.

Example

The destroyed$ observable allows consumers to react to FeatureCell teardown. This is typically used to clean up subscriptions, release external resources, or coordinate higher-level lifecycle behavior.

Example: Observing FeatureCell Destruction

{{`this.vault.destroyed$
  .subscribe(() => {
    console.info('FeatureCell has been destroyed');
  });`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.destroyed$
  .subscribe(() => {
    console.info('FeatureCell has been destroyed');
  });`}}

What this does

  • Subscribes to the FeatureCell destruction signal
  • Receives a single notification when destruction occurs
  • Automatically completes after emitting
  • Does not receive state values or snapshots

This stream is ideal for teardown coordination and cleanup logic that must run exactly once when the FeatureCell lifecycle ends.
